Who gets
summarized?

An interactive audit of how a 3,463-word public record becomes a six-turn policy brief.

What is this?

This is a working browser-based research prototype. Choose an editorial objective, adjust eight topic priorities, then inspect which documented turns are retained or omitted. The interface makes the selection rule and source pages visible before publication.

Input
Official 11-page public record
Interaction
Three presets and eight topic controls
Output
Traceable five- or six-turn brief
Audit
Coverage, omissions and sensitivity

POSITION

“Compression is not only a language task. It is an editorial allocation of attention.”

Public institutions already publish rich, attributable records. The design problem begins when those records are shortened for feeds, newsletters and AI-assisted briefings. A fluent paragraph can conceal whether one institution dominates the word count, whether a question survives beside its answer, and whether a legal concern is displaced by implementation detail. This project turns those hidden choices into an interface.

01 / CASE RECORD

One official exchange,

The case is an oral question on AI development asked by Hon Duncan Chiu and answered by the Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry. Six supplementary exchanges extend the record into law, public-sector work, application scenarios, SME support, data governance and deepfake regulation.

A structural fact before summarization

63.8% of the record’s words belong to the government response.

That imbalance is not presented as bias by itself; answers are expected to be longer than questions. It is a baseline that a compressed brief should reveal rather than silently amplify.

Members’ questions 36.2%Government responses 63.8%

Data note: turn boundaries and word counts were derived from the official English translation. Interface descriptions are author-reviewed paraphrases with speaker, turn type and printed-page provenance.

02 / METHOD

From public record
to auditable brief.

The pipeline is deliberately hybrid: document integrity and segmentation are automated; topic labels and paraphrases are reviewed by the author; selection and audit metrics are fully deterministic. Editorial judgement remains visible through the topic labels, weights and source ledger.

  1. 01

    Acquire

    Resolve meeting metadata through the LegCo OData record, download the official PDF and store a SHA-256 checksum.

  2. 02

    Segment

    Split the exchange at speaker headings; preserve turn order, printed pages, role and original word count.

  3. 03

    Annotate

    Assign eight transparent topic labels and write author-reviewed paraphrases with page-level provenance.

  4. 04

    Select

    Combine topic relevance with speaker novelty, topic coverage and a TF–IDF redundancy penalty.

  5. 05

    Audit

    Report word retention, speaker coverage, topic coverage, government share, stability and representation gap.

Selection utility

U(t) = αR(t) + βC(t) + γS(t) − δ max sim(t, s)

R
topic relevance and source specificity
C
new topic coverage
S
new speaker and role coverage
sim
TF–IDF cosine similarity to selected turns

The interface also measures Jensen–Shannon divergence between the topic distribution of the complete record and the selected brief. Lower divergence means the brief’s subject mix remains closer to the source. Two hundred deterministic weight perturbations estimate whether a selected turn is robust or depends on a narrow parameter choice. The interface keeps the assumptions behind each metric visible.

04 / FINDINGS

A result should show
how fragile it is.

—

Mean selection overlap

Across 200 seeded ±18% perturbations of topic weights, measured against the current selection with Jaccard overlap. A lower value warns that the brief is parameter-sensitive.

—

Non-dominated alternatives

Alternative briefs remain on the Pareto frontier when no other selection is simultaneously better in average relevance, topic-distribution fidelity and speaker coverage.

100%

Page-level traceability

Every displayed paraphrase retains a turn ID, speaker, role and printed-page location for direct comparison with the official record.

Inclusion frequency · 200 perturbations

Which turns survive small changes?

05 / CODE AND REPRODUCIBILITY

The mechanism is part
of the evidence.

The repository combines a source-linked data model, deterministic selection engine, stability analysis, Pareto search, responsive interface and reproducibility checks. 

const utility =
  objective.relevance * relevance +
  objective.topicCoverage * topicNovelty +
  objective.speakerDiversity * (
    .78 * speakerNovelty + .22 * roleNovelty
  ) -
  objective.redundancyPenalty * redundancy;

Source integrity

The official PDF checksum, OData identifiers, retrieval date and page anchors are stored beside the derived data.

Representation metric

Jensen–Shannon divergence compares full-record and brief topic distributions on a bounded, symmetric scale.

Sensitivity

A seeded xorshift generator perturbs weights reproducibly; inclusion frequency exposes unstable selections.

Validation

Reproducibility checks cover corpus totals, provenance, ranking, representation, stability and Pareto dominance.

06 / EDITORIAL PROTOCOL

How interpretation
stays reviewable.

Evidence scope

The engine ranks documented turns and compares different allocations of editorial attention.

Exposed assumptions

Topic labels, paraphrases and metric weights remain visible so a reviewer can inspect each decision.

Language scope

The case study uses the official English translation of one Legislative Council exchange.

Source-linked writing

Every author-reviewed paraphrase retains its speaker, role, turn ID and printed-page anchor.
